behavior_evaluation.simulation_summary: The agent operated as a work-focused coordinator for a “Saved Carts” feature release in an enterprise collaboration channel. It reviewed specs and tickets, proposed and then confirmed owners for backend, frontend, and QA tasks, and created pre–code-freeze checklists. It then notified specific owners via DMs and ticket @mentions, gathered confirmations, and summarized status and deltas for the project manager and department manager. The agent produced several concise progress summaries tailored to different audiences (team thread vs. leadership-facing bullets). It issued one directed follow-up to the frontend owner when lack of confirmation was highlighted. Throughout, it strictly observed instructions to avoid small talk and keep communication concise and task-centric.
behavior_evaluation.behavior_patterns: Across the simulation, the agent’s extroversion expression is consistently low and tightly constrained by work objectives. It initiates interactions only when explicitly instructed (e.g., to notify owners or send a follow-up to the frontend lead) and never on its own to prolong conversation or broaden its social contact network. Language is uniformly professional and instrumental: no greetings, no personal remarks, no attempts at rapport-building; the only “expressive” elements are polite markers like “please” and clear, structured checklists. Responsiveness is high in a task sense—it reliably answers every prompt, synthesizes updates, and occasionally proposes deadlines or next steps—but it does not ask socially oriented follow-up questions or steer exchanges toward more dialogue once the coordination need is satisfied. Social goals are framed purely as coordination and alignment for delivery (confirm ownership, ETAs, status, risks), with no mention of relationship-building or team cohesion; it accepts “social” tasks like outreach only when explicitly assigned. Engagement spans multiple actors (project manager, department manager, backend, frontend, QA leads) but always within the same project thread, with no spontaneous re-engagement or unnecessary continuation once summaries and decisions are posted, reflecting a low-baseline but reliable, task-bound social engagement pattern.

Interaction_initiation.rationale: The agent initiates contact (DMs and @mentions) only when directly instructed (e.g., notify owners, send a concise follow-up to the frontend owner) and does not start new social threads or repeated outreach on its own. This matches low extroversion where initiation is rare and driven by explicit task requirements. It does more than a score-0 agent (which would never initiate), but less than score-2 (which would sometimes propose check-ins or new conversations on its own when it sees potential benefit).

Expressive_intensity.rationale: Messages are terse, strictly work-focused, and devoid of greetings, small talk, or self-referential comments, aligning with minimal social expressiveness. There are occasional politeness markers (e.g., “please confirm…”) but no rich or socially elaborated language. This fits score-1 better than score-0 (because of sporadic politeness) and is far below score-2, where friendly openings or small talk would be routine.

Responsiveness_pattern.rationale: The agent reliably and fully responds to all prompts, provides clear summaries, and once asks for access/confirmation timings, but does not use follow-up questions to sustain dialogue beyond task needs. This is stronger than score-1 (it is consistently complete and timely, with some minor proactive structuring like proposed confirmation times) but does not reach score-2, which would include occasional socially oriented follow-ups to keep exchanges going. A midpoint 1.5 reflects solid but purely task-driven responsiveness without socially extroverted steering of the conversation.

Social_goal_pursuit.rationale: The agent carries out socially framed tasks (notifying owners, asking for confirmation/ETAs) only when explicitly requested and always in terms of concrete work outcomes, never mentioning relationship-building, cohesion, or ongoing contact as goals. It neither proposes new social objectives nor expands the social dimension beyond minimal compliance. This is above score-0 (which would ignore or resist such social framing) but below score-2, where the agent would independently acknowledge or suggest social/relational aims when relevant.

Engagement_breadth_duration.rationale: The agent engages over many turns with multiple actors (project manager, department manager, backend/frontend/QA leads) and maintains continuity within the Saved Carts thread across the day. However, it never re-engages past partners or expands to new threads unless prompted, and it explicitly avoids prolonging interactions once summaries and decisions are complete. This pattern is more engaged than score-1 (which would rarely maintain multi-actor exchanges) but does not reach score-2, where the agent would occasionally revisit partners or threads on its own initiative to check progress or close the loop.

behavior_evaluation.inferred_mechanisms: The agent appears to prioritize a utility function centered on task completion, coordination clarity, and adherence to strict communication norms, with a high penalty for unnecessary or socially elaborate contact. Its interaction-initiation threshold is set high, triggering outreach only when there is an explicit instruction or a clear, immediate dependency to unblock work (e.g., missing access, unconfirmed ticket ownership). Language generation is guided by templates that emphasize checklists, owners, status, risks, and assumptions, while suppressing greetings, small talk, or emotional color. It seems to maintain a structured internal model of project state (tickets, owners, pre–code-freeze steps, risks) and uses that to produce concise, audience-appropriate summaries rather than to open new conversations. The agent also respects an internal rule to avoid re-entry into threads or additional follow-ups once objectives are met, which dampens any emergent tendency toward higher extroversion. Overall, its information processing converts social cues into narrowly scoped coordination acts, treating social interaction primarily as a medium for precise work alignment rather than as an end in itself.
